<description>
Picks up #28538

Outbound-full-relay slots should be used by peers that actually relay transactions, besides #28538 see #16418 and #28371 for the motivation. So try to replace peers that are not relaying txs with peers that do.

The approach differs from the original PR in a few details in response to some of the review comments there:

- A replacement is connected before the peer is evicted. The original PR disconnected a non-tx-relaying peer once all full outbound slots were filled. Reviewers preferred having a replacement available first (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). Now an extra outbound-full-relay connection is requested, like the extra network-specific peers, and the existing eviction of extra outbound peers prefers peers that don't relay txs.
- Peers not relaying txs don't get `m_protect`. Otherwise they could stay forever (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443336121), and ignoring the protection was rejected in the same thread (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443312604).
- An only peer on a network is not replaced. Otherwise the network-specific extra connections and this logic would keep replacing each other (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). This also covers the `-maxconnections=1` case (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1417178196).

Nothing is changed in `-blocksonly` mode or during IBD. The rename commit and the functional test are taken from the original PR with some changes to match the new behavior.
</description>

[2026-11-27] c:7217866150 comment by Bicaru20 (contributor) (edited 2026-11-27):
ACK 5c8457a367e810a99d3784bec275f8cc0fe76cdb

I was worried that this new behaviour could isolate the blocksonly node. Specifically I wonder what would happen if one of those nodes wanted to send a transaction. But after thinking a little bit I saw that it would propagate normally since the blocksonly nodes can also choose their peers, so as long as they have one peer that is not blocksonly there is no problem. Still, I ran a small experiment to see how the normal nodes now change look for peers that are not blocksonly and also to see if the propagation of transactions is afected.

Experiment:

The experiment consist on 6 nodes an a regtest. From nodes 1 to 3 are normal and nodes from 4 to 6 are `blocksonly`. Their initials connections where (I limited the outbound connection to 2):
- Node 1 → 2, 4
- Node 2 → 3, 5
- Node 3 → 1, 6
- Node 4 → 2, 5
- Node 5 → 3, 6
- Node 6 → 1, 4

That way I could see if node 1 to 3 would change their `blocksonly` peers for normal peers. This is what I got:

(_The image has been generated with gemini. I directly passed the logs of the info I collected to the agent to generate this graph_)

The first and second node where able to connect to normal nodes very quickly. For some reason for a short time they connected again to a blockonly node. I had some issues with node 3 during that time so probably that is the issue. The node 3 took longer to connect to just normal nodes but evetually it also got there. I also checked that before disconnecting from a blocksonly they always had already the new connection.

Since I already had build this setup, I also tried to brodcast a trasnaction from one of the blockonly nodes with `sendrawtransaction` and there was no problem with the transaction arriving to the others nodes.

This is a very small experiment but it was just to see that the pr works as expected :)
</new_statements>
